title: Cross-entity session-stitch + fingerprinted invocation mart for cost and latency joins
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a curated, query-optimized invocation mart that stitches user-level and system-level events across services (API gateway, routing, model runtime) using deterministic fingerprinting. Goal: support low-latency joins for per-route cost and latency attribution in Console dashboards and alerting. This ticket covers schema design, ETL logic (stitching & de-dup), sparse storage strategy, partitioning, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Daily mart produced with <=2% duplication on sampled invocations.
2) Common queries (per-workspace per-route 7d cost/latency) run < 2s on BI cluster.
3) Costs and latency figures match existing realtime pipeline within +/-5% on sample tenants.
4) Rollout toggle and backfill scripts in place; docs and field-level data contract published.
tasks: Design fingerprinting strategy (fields, hash algorithm, salt policy)
Define canonical event stream ordering & tie-breaks for session stitching
Implement Spark ETL job: join API gateway events -> routing -> runtime traces
Add Sparse partitioned storage (weekly partitions + compacted delta snapshots)
Write backfill + reconciliation job and validation notebook
Add CI checks (schema evolution tests) and alerting for data skew
Document data contract and register mart in Console data catalog
schema_preview: columns: workspace_id, fingerprint_id, invocation_id, route_id, model_variant, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, latency_ms, source_event_types, session_score, dedup_flag, partition_week
decisions: 1) Use xxh3_64 as fingerprint hash for speed and low collision rate. 2) Salt per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant collisions and support export controls. 3) Employ weekly partition + compacted delta snapshots instead of hourly partitions to reduce small-file pressure on object store. 4) Keep canonicalization deterministic: ordering by (event_ts, upstream_seq, instance_id).
